title: weeklyOSM 844
content:
17/09/2026-23/09/2026

[1] A map of Ohio highlighting 1,309 township boundary areas. | OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles | Map data © by OpenStreetMap Contributors.

  • Next week we will launch our completely revamped website; an exciting milestone for us! With Hugo as our new framework, a self-hosted commenting system (Remark42), and our own Listmonk server for managing mailing lists, we’ve modernised our publishing workflow and automated key processes. The source code is available, along with the complete archive in Markdown format, in the FOSSGIS GitLab repository. Cross your fingers for a smooth transition.
  • [1] After almost 15 years, mappers in the US state of Ohio have finished mapping the boundaries of all 1,309 townships there. The community overcame a lack of accurate, authoritative, external datasets by reconciling a variety of sources. Work remains to clean up and update municipal boundaries, which often influence township boundaries.
  • Walid Nouh has interviewed members of the OpenStreetMap France board on the Projets Libres podcast. The episode’s guests were asked to talk about OSM-FR, who they are, what the association does, and its current activities.

title: weeklyOSM 843
content:
10/09/2026-16/09/2026

  • v7.2.0 of the iD tagging schema has been released and includes tweaks to labels, new icons, changed fields for various presets, new search terms, better documentation, improved build scripts, and more. Helper presets for some subvariants of aerialway stations, silos, and parking spots were added to make mapping easier. An actual new preset was added for offshore platforms. It includes bugfixes such as dropping bad suggestions, taginfo report includes addTags, and post boxes in USA no longer have duplicate drivethrough fields. Work continues in the background on some larger features, but changes listed above will soon be present in iD, GoMap!!, EveryDoor, StreetComplete, and other editors.

  • Andy Allan gave a talk at State of the Map 2026 about how OpenStreetMap’s transport layer migrated from server-side rendered map tiles to client-side rendered vector styles.

title: weeklyOSM 840
content:
20/08/2026-26/08/2026

  • In early August, v7.1.0 of the iD tagging schema was released, bringing new features to iD, GoMap!!, EveryDoor, and other editors. It includes multiple new presets (for example, for rooftop solar thermal collectors and building=tent), marks some fields as openinghours-like, new values in fields such as cuisine, some region-specific tweaks, many better icons, fixes destination fields, and stops asking translators to translate the same phrase twice in many places, also better documentation, better repository structure, and many other improvements.

  • A poll by Mateusz Konieczny asks which improvements to iD presets are especially wanted.

title: weeklyOSM 839
content:
13/08/2026-19/08/2026

  • The proposal for revising lgbtq=* , authored by Spughetti, aims to make tagging of LGBTQ+ features more accurate. It does so by deprecating keys that don’t provide added information over existing keys, changing the formatting of keys, and introducing new sub-keys. The RFC period started on 12 August 2026.

    • A proposal, authored by Biff, suggests extending the highway=traffic_mirror node with a relation type=traffic_mirror that specifies how the traffic mirror is intended to be used for the specific highway. It extends the already defined role=from and role=to members of the relation, provides better guidance for their meaning and the selection of their location, and also covers additional situations such as bidirectional mirrors on curves and dead-angle mirrors. Additionally, the proposal defines a new and recommended role=visible member to indicate relevant ways (or nodes) that can be seen through the traffic mirror. The RFC period is open until 12 September 2026.

  • Rphyrin developed Warlok, a web tool for identifying the top OSM contributors in a specific local neighbourhood.

title: weeklyOSM 838
content:
06/08/2026-12/08/2026

  • SherbetS has proposed craft=meat_processing for small-scale facilities where hunters or animal owners bring a carcass to be cut into meat, as distinct from shop=butcher or industrial=slaughterhouse. RFC voting started on 30 July. The proposal grew out of an earlier discussion on how to tag deer processors, where commenters debated craft=butcher, man_made=works, and various animal-specific alternatives before settling on the more general wording. In the RFC thread, several contributors argued that craft=butcher would fit just as well and that ‘meat processing’ sounds too industrial in British English, while others worried the new tag could end up being used for large commercial plants too.

title: weeklyOSM 836
content:
23/07/2026-29/07/2026

  • [1] Les Libres Géographes has shared a methodology called OSM Skeleton, which aims to reduce the heterogeneity of OpenStreetMap data to create a coherent and locally maintainable common dataset of geographic references. The approach systematically identifies, on a national scale, missing, incomplete, inaccurate, or obsolete features among those considered fundamental: place nodes, road network, and residential areas. It uses a hybrid feature called ‘urban areas’ for analytical purposes. In particular, it generates WMS layers of alerts, instruction pages for easily correcting them in JOSM or iD, tracking statistics, and also a score for the density of POIs in towns. Séverin Ménard will present it at the upcoming SotM in Paris.
